facilitatorNotes: Four containers, four answers (or a dartboard with four zones, decided on the spot per venue). Keep it quick and light, with no scores.

Problem owner explains the PaG and answers questions. Centre word: "creativity knowledge" — confirmed after the mentor session. Prompt the RG twice: once for what's written down (books, named techniques), once for what only passes by example (a mindset, the kind of thing Mark gave students that's in no book).

RG was tired after a full day — kept to 8 minutes, well under the book's usual range. Facilitator helps if the RG is slow. Aim for 3 to 6 families; a rest cluster is fine. Many distinct clusters → all go forward to How-To's; few, similar clusters → pick the most outstanding.

Default: many clusters → many How-To's, to diverge as much as possible. Few, similar clusters → How-To's only for the most outstanding ones. If the RG stalls after 3 minutes, offer one of the three fallback PaPs. Problem owner confirms the PaP is relevant before it's read aloud and written large.
Read a few aloud, no discussion. This empties the obvious so the excursion isn't spent regenerating it.

Cool evening outdoors ruled out running the whole session outside, so stayed with Random Words rather than Random Objects. Draw the word with the PaP out of sight; chain each new word from the last answer, not just one layer deep.
Pass drawings around and build on them. MATEC was dropped as too complex for this case; mentor confirmed force fitting plus brainsketching as the better combination after the excursion.

Axes: value creation for students vs. student engagement. Sem said he can make a crazy idea work himself, so use a joker card or dot to protect one bold, low-scoring idea. Sem names the options he takes forward and wants something tangible to hand over — a poster or a booklet.
Thank the RG. Sem reacts as problem owner. Agree what the client receives afterward — the client report needs this agreement up front. Keep the PaP, C-box and chosen idea visible on the wall.
Each participant answers alone, then shares. Ask Sem to reflect too.
